findings.failure_scenario: GET /login: LoginPage (apps/web/app/login/page.tsx) server-renders <LoginForm/>, so `localStorage.getItem("theme")` runs in Node 20 (the version pinned in package.json engines) where localStorage is undefined → `ReferenceError: localStorage is not defined` → the sign-in page returns a 500 instead of the form. Even in the browser the value is always null (nothing ever calls localStorage.setItem("theme"); DynamicSharedLayout writes the js-cookie "theme" cookie instead), so the dark-mode branch can never activate.
findings.summary: Client component reads localStorage during render, which throws during Next.js server rendering of /login.

findings.failure_scenario: Any request, e.g. https://custom.example.com/s/abc, has pathname "/s/abc" (truthy), so the middleware returns `NextResponse.next()` immediately. Unverified/unknown custom domains are no longer redirected to cap.so, the `verified_domain` cache cookie is never set, and the Access-Control-* headers for /api/* on custom domains are never emitted, breaking CORS for every custom-domain API call.
findings.summary: New `if (path)` early return always fires (url.pathname is never empty), making every custom-domain check below it unreachable.

findings.failure_scenario: The comment textarea is `bg-gray-1` + `text-gray-1` (both #fcfcfc in the light theme), so a signed-in user types a comment and sees nothing. The same remap hides previously dark text in EmptyCapState.tsx:21 ("Hey! Record your first Cap"), DocsPage.tsx:33/42, CustomDomain.tsx:323/329/357 (Type/Name/Value labels), Logo.tsx:65/74 (version label) and Transcript.tsx:251/295.
findings.summary: Old dark text colors were remapped to `gray-1`, the lightest surface token in the new Radix scale, so the text becomes invisible on light backgrounds.

findings.failure_scenario: apps/desktop/tailwind.config.js loads @cap/ui-solid/tailwind, whose theme defines only gray-50..500/blue-50..400 — there is no gray-1 or gray-8 key, so `bg-gray-1` and `disabled:text-gray-8` emit no CSS in the desktop build: the `white`-variant Export button (apps/desktop/src/routes/recordings-overlay.tsx:370) loses its background, and disabled buttons (e.g. apps/desktop/src/routes/(window-chrome)/settings/hotkeys.tsx:169) keep their enabled text color instead of the disabled one. SwitchTab.tsx:21/38 has the same undefined tokens (currently unused export).
findings.summary: Classes renamed to gray-1/gray-8 tokens that do not exist in the Tailwind config consumed by the desktop app, so the utilities are never generated.

findings.failure_scenario: The dashboard nav renders `<button class="mt-3 w-full"><button class="…">Add new space</button></button>`; the HTML parser closes the outer button before the inner one, so React logs a hydration mismatch (React 18 validateDOMNesting) and the click that should open the create-space dialog can fire on both the inner button and the outer trigger.
findings.summary: Radix DialogTrigger (renders a <button>) now wraps a Button component ({variant="dark"}) that also renders a <button>, producing invalid nested buttons.

findings.failure_scenario: `<Logo white />` at apps/web/app/s/[videoId]/_components/ShareVideo.tsx:1432 (the watermark drawn over the video player) renders the "Cap" wordmark with `var(--gray-12)` (near-black in the light theme) instead of #ffffff, so the watermark is dark/wrong over video content; the class wins over `fill={white ? "#ffffff" : "#12161F"}` for every caller.
findings.summary: Added `className="fill-gray-12"` overrides the SVG `fill` presentation attribute, so the `white` prop no longer applies to the wordmark.

findings.failure_scenario: Collapse the sidebar (or press Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+S) and reload the dashboard: `useState(false)` always re-expands it while line 17 keeps writing localStorage, so the persisted preference is never read and the sidebar snaps back on every load/navigation.
findings.summary: Initial collapse state no longer restores the persisted `sidebarCollapsed` value that toggleCollapse still writes.

findings.failure_scenario: On /dashboard with a theme=dark cookie, `headers().get("x-current-path")` returns undefined (middleware only does `response.headers.set`, which is not visible to `headers()`) → `isPathDashboard` is falsy → `<body className="light">` is server-rendered and the `theme` cookie read at lines 49-50 is dead code, so dark-mode users see a flash of the light theme until DynamicSharedLayout's client effect applies the cookie.
findings.summary: The layout reads `x-current-path` from request headers, but middleware sets it on the response, so `isPathDashboard` is always undefined.

findings.failure_scenario: A space whose custom domain DNS is not verified: SharedCapCard now delegates to CapCard and links to `https://<unverified-domain>/s/<id>`; the previous SharedCapCard code required `activeSpace.space.domainVerified` and fell back to cap.link/NEXT_PUBLIC_WEB_URL, so shared-cap links now point at a host that does not serve the app.
findings.summary: capUrl now checks only `activeSpace.space.customDomain`; the `domainVerified` guard the shared-cap card used to apply was dropped.

findings.failure_scenario: Dead code introduced by the change: a repo-wide search for `setTheme` finds only DynamicSharedLayout's unrelated state setter/setThemeHandler and the desktop Tauri command, so this module adds a second, untested cookie-writing path (without expiry) that nothing uses; the file also has no trailing newline.
findings.summary: New "use server" setTheme action is never imported or called anywhere; the theme is actually written by js-cookie inside DynamicSharedLayout.

findings.failure_scenario: For a TableCell containing `[role=checkbox]`, `selection:[&:has([role=checkbox])]:pr-0` compiles to a `::selection` descendant rule instead of the previous `[&:has([role=checkbox])]:pr-0`, so the cell keeps the default p-2 padding and the intended right-padding/translate adjustments no longer apply to checkbox selects.
findings.summary: A `selection:` variant was accidentally prefixed to the checkbox-cell padding reset, turning it into a ::selection rule that never matches.

findings.failure_scenario: React may invoke a state updater more than once (StrictMode double-invoke in dev) or discard a render, so `animateDirection`/`previousCountRef` are mutated for updates that never commit while `newSelection.length > prev.length` is computed from the double-invocation; `previousCountRef.current` (line 102) has no reader anywhere, so it is dead state.
findings.summary: setAnimateDirection (and a previousCountRef write) is invoked inside the setSelectedCaps updater, which React requires to be pure — and previousCountRef is never read.

findings.failure_scenario: Tailwind preflight sets border-width: 0, and the class string "relative p-6 w-full max-w-lg rounded-xl shadow-lg bg-gray-7 border-gray-9" contains no border-width class, so every dialog renders without the intended gray-9 outline (the old class set had no border either, so the newly added color token never takes effect).
findings.summary: DialogContent sets `border-gray-9` but no `border`/`border-[1px]` width utility, so the border color is a no-op.

findings.failure_scenario: With theme === "dark", AdminMobileNav line 65 renders faSun while DashboardInner line 67 renders faMoon for the identical state and click behaviour; one of the two toggles therefore displays the wrong glyph (state indicator vs. action target), giving contradictory affordances in the same app.
findings.summary: Desktop and mobile theme toggles use opposite icon semantics for the same state.

findings.failure_scenario: All four emails render `<Tailwind>` with no custom config (React Email uses Tailwind's default theme, which has gray-50..950 but no gray-1), so `bg-gray-1` produces no CSS and the Body background silently reverts to the mail client's default — in dark-mode or non-white clients the message loses the intended white body. Same change in first-shareable-link.tsx:29, new-comment.tsx:35 and workspace-invite.tsx:31.
findings.summary: Email bodies switched from `bg-white` to `bg-gray-1`, a token that React Email's default Tailwind theme does not contain, so no background rule is emitted.
